title: Budget ceilings graded two-sided: an under-budget artifact fails acceptance
body:
## Summary
Four balance steps grade a CEILING (load ms, decoded MB, GPU ms, shader instructions) with withinPercent, a two-sided band, so a cheaper/faster artifact fails and the fail reason tells the producer to spend more.

## Description
withinPercent (src/lib/catalog/acceptance/dataCheckers.ts:122-130) passes only inside target*(1±pct). It is used as a budget ceiling at src/lib/catalog/pipelines/save-points.ts:593 (30 ms ±50% -> a 10 ms load fails), src/lib/catalog/pipelines/ambient.ts:672 (label says "Total decoded ≤8 MB" but 3 MB fails), src/lib/catalog/pipelines/vfx.ts:231 (0.48 ms ±15% -> a 0.3 ms effect fails) and src/lib/catalog/pipelines/materials.ts:327 (200 ±20% -> a 140-instruction shader fails). Each step ALSO composes budgetWithinCap against its declared cap, so the ceiling is enforced twice and the floor is the only thing the literal adds. Same family: src/lib/catalog/pipelines/vendors.ts:375 repeats a literal 30 next to the declared economySim.marginTargetPct it already grades. Fixed looks like a ceiling-only checker (atMost(field,label,canonCeiling)) in dataCheckers.ts, swapped in at the four budget sites; rate targets (loot-tables raresPerHour) stay two-sided. Technique: acceptance-verdict-spine hardcoded-pass-antipattern mirror - a grader whose verdict contradicts its own label.

## Flow
- live produce for a lean entity writes measuredMs 10 / totalDecodedMb 3 / gpuMs 0.3 / instructionCount 140
- allOf -> withinPercent -> status fail, reason "10 is outside ±50% of 30"
- fix: add atMost to dataCheckers.ts (catalog-acceptance), replace the 4 withinPercent ceiling calls, keep budgetWithinCap

## Expected impact
Live CLI produces for cheaper-than-exemplar content stop failing and stop being coached to inflate cost; measured as the 4 under-budget probes flipping fail->pass while over-budget probes still fail. Could break: a pinned acceptance label string in a snapshot test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a budget step passes every artifact under its ceiling and fails every one over it
Before: probe over the seeded entity with the value lowered: save-points/Load-Time Budget, ambient/Memory Budget, vfx/GPU / LOD Budget, materials/LOD/Perf Budget all pass->fail (4 of 4 under-budget artifacts fail)
After: predicted 0 of 4 fail under atMost; over-budget control (value x1.6) still fails 4 of 4
Method: probe - mutated each produced artifact in a throwaway vitest and graded it with the registered checker; After needs the new checker in src/lib/catalog/acceptance (out of this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
UNDERBUDGET save-points/Load-Time Budget: before=pass after=fail reason=10 is outside ±50% of 30
UNDERBUDGET ambient/Memory Budget: before=pass after=fail reason=3 is outside ±33% of 6
UNDERBUDGET vfx/GPU / LOD Budget: before=pass after=fail reason=0.3 is outside ±15% of 0.48
UNDERBUDGET materials/LOD/Perf Budget: before=pass after=fail reason=140 is outside ±20% of 200
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/ambient.ts:672 withinPercent('totalDecodedMb', 'Total decoded ≤8 MB (within ±33% of 6 MB target)', 6.0, 33)
instrument: a test grading each of the 4 steps with value x0.5 (must pass) and x1.6 (must fail), red today on the x0.5 half

title: Lossy asset slug in 28 pipelines: a non-ASCII name emits BP_/NS_/ACH_ with no token
body:
## Summary
28 pipeline files each define slug = n.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, ""), the lossy form Items already replaced with a collision-safe itemSlug; a name with no ASCII letters yields an empty slug and bare-prefix UE asset names that collide across entities.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/itemAssetPaths.ts:51 itemSlug returns Item_<idToken> for an empty readable slug and appends a token on collision, because "Iron Sword"/"Iron-Sword" collapse. The other 28 copies (e.g. src/lib/catalog/pipelines/vfx.ts:11, bestiary.ts:15, achievements.ts:11, combat-map.ts:17 ... 28 sites by grep) keep the lossy form, so two entities named "影の刃" and "炎の剣" both produce BP_, NS_, ACH_ and the same UE paths. The {slug} token in contract declarations is filled by a third copy, src/lib/catalog/contractPrompt.ts:112, which must change in lockstep (out of this context). Fixed: one shared entitySlug(name,id) beside itemSlug, used by all 28 files and contractPrompt fill; ASCII-unique names keep byte-identical output.

## Flow
- create an entity whose name has no ASCII letters
- produce any of 17 pipelines -> asset names like "BP_ inherits AARPGEnemy", "NS_", "ACH_"
- fix: shared slug helper (non-empty, collision-token), adopt in 28 files + contractPrompt.ts:112

## Expected impact
Non-English or symbol-named entities stop sharing one UE path; measured as the empty-slug probe count. Could break: any pinned produce output for a name whose slug changes (none of the seeded ASCII names).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every produced UE asset name carries a non-empty, entity-unique slug
Before: probe: name "影の刃" over every registered pipeline -> 58 steps in 17 pipelines emit a bare-prefix asset token; 28 duplicated slug definitions vs 1 fixed (itemSlug)
After: predicted 0 bare-prefix steps; seeded-entity produce output byte-identical (0 of N changed)
Method: probe - ran every step produce for a synthetic non-ASCII entity in a throwaway vitest and regex-matched bare prefixes; After needs the shared helper plus contractPrompt.ts (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep "^const slug = (n: string) => n.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, '')" src/lib/catalog/pipelines -> 28 files
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts:26 const slug = (e: LabEntity) => itemSlug(e);
src/lib/catalog/contractPrompt.ts:112 text.split('{slug}').join(entity.name.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, ''))
probe: EMPTYSLUG 58 lines across 17 catalogs (vfx 6, props 7, materials 6, screen-flow 6, ...)
instrument: a test producing every pipeline for two distinct non-ASCII names asserting no bare-prefix token and no shared asset path, plus a byte-identity check for every seeded entity

title: Vendors produce ships "TODO: ... when the sim gate lands" though the sim exists
body:
## Summary
The vendors Economy Sim step writes a TODO into the produced artifact (simNotes) saying the economy simulator has not landed; pof_economy_simulate and pof_combat_simulate are registered pof-mcp tools.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/vendors.ts:363 puts "TODO: replace the analytic buyer-mix with a pof_economy_simulate run when the sim gate lands." into economySim.simNotes, which the View shows and the artifact persists. tools/pof-mcp/src/tools/sims.ts and tools/pof-mcp/src/coverage.ts:20-21 register both simulators, exercised by tools/pof-mcp/src/quality.itest.ts:103,116. The same claim sits as a comment at src/lib/catalog/pipelines/combat-map.ts:557. Fixed: either wire a simulator-backed checker (the real fix) or reword the shipped note to state the margin is analytic and name the available tool; never a TODO in produced content.

## Flow
- open vendors > Economy Sim in /layout
- View renders simNotes ending in a TODO that asserts a missing gate
- fix: reword simNotes (S) or add a sim-backed checker (L)

## Expected impact
The operator reading the step stops being told a tool is missing; a sim-backed grade would replace an analytic margin. Could break: nothing graded reads simNotes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - produced artifact copy states only what is true of the tree
Before: 1 TODO string in produced artifact data (vendors simNotes); 2 simulators registered in tools/pof-mcp
After: 0 TODO strings in produced data (scan over every step produce output)
Method: probe - grep of produced data strings plus the pof-mcp registration; the real fix (sim-backed grade) is L and needs the director to choose
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/vendors.ts:363 'TODO: replace the analytic buyer-mix with a pof_economy_simulate run when the sim gate lands.'
tools/pof-mcp/src/coverage.ts:20 pof_combat_simulate
tools/pof-mcp/src/coverage.ts:21 pof_economy_simulate
instrument: a test walking every pipeline produce output for strings matching /\bTODO\b/ (comments stripped by construction - it reads data), red today on vendors Economy Sim

title: Corrupt council seats.json reads as "seats.json unrecorded"
body:
## Summary
readCouncilFacts swallows a JSON parse error of seats.json and reports zero seats, so the Council verdict says "seats.json unrecorded" for a file that exists but is corrupt.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/contracts/contractsReadCouncil.ts:19-25 readJson returns null on any error; parseSeats(null) is [] (src/lib/catalog/pipelines/contracts/contractsParse.ts:182-191), and src/lib/catalog/acceptance/contractsCheckers.ts:45 renders "seats.json unrecorded". Absent and corrupt are one state; the run still passes. The sibling reads in contractsRead.ts distinguish present+error (readJsonFile returns {present,error}). Fixed: CouncilFacts gains seatsError, read with the same present/error shape, and the checker names it.

## Flow
- a council run folder whose seats.json is truncated
- Council passes with "seats.json unrecorded"
- fix: carry the parse error into CouncilFacts and the detail

## Expected impact
A broken council record is visible on the Council step instead of reading as never written. Could break: snapshot byte-identity (a new key) re-archives Council once.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a present-but-corrupt seats.json is reported as corrupt
Before: walked: truncated seats.json -> seats [] -> detail "seats.json unrecorded" (same as no file)
After: detail names "seats.json unreadable: <error>"
Method: simulation - traced readJson -> parseSeats -> councilFacts; checker change is in catalog-acceptance (out of scope), so not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/contracts/contractsReadCouncil.ts:19-25 function readJson(file) { try { return JSON.parse(...) } catch { return null; } }
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/contractsCheckers.ts:45 const seats = c.seats.length ? ... : 'seats.json unrecorded';
instrument: a contracts fixture test writing seats.json as "{ nope" and asserting the Council detail names it unreadable

title: Player-movement copy claims an 8-way, 11-clip blend grid; the module builds 4-way from 9
body:
## Summary
The Blend Space Grid checker label says "11-sample 8-way strafe grid" and its produceNote says "Wires 11 retargeted clips"; the UE module builds 11 samples from 9 distinct clips at 0/±90/±180 only - no diagonals.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/player-movement.ts:90-91 vs the UE project module Content/Python/player_movement/build_blend_space.py GRID (lines 25-39): Idle + walk ring (0, 90, -90, 180, -180) + run ring (same), with Walking_Backwards and Running_Backward each used twice. 0 of the 4 diagonal directions (±45, ±135) an 8-way grid has are present. Fixed: the label/note say "11-sample 4-direction grid from 9 clips", or the module gains diagonals - an owner choice about the feel.

## Flow
- read the Blend Space Grid step in /layout
- copy promises diagonal strafing the built asset does not have
- fix: correct label + produceNote (S) or add diagonal clips (UE work)

## Expected impact
An operator stops expecting diagonal blends that are not authored. Could break: nothing; checker count 11 stays.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - step copy matches the asset the module builds
Before: "8-way" claimed; 0 of 4 diagonals in GRID; "11 retargeted clips" claimed vs 9 distinct
After: copy states 4 directions, 9 clips, 11 samples
Method: probe - read both sources; the UE module lives in the UE repo (separate tree), so no in-repo gate can pin the parity
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/player-movement.ts:90 accept: pythonStepSuccess('11-sample 8-way strafe grid in BS_Locomotion', 11)
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/player-movement.ts:91 produceNote: 'Wires 11 retargeted clips into BS_Locomotion'
build_blend_space.py GRID: (0,0,Standard_Idle),(0/90/-90/180/-180, WALK),(0/90/-90/180/-180, RUN)
instrument: a parity check reading the UE GRID through the existing UE-root resolver (skip when no UE root) and asserting the step copy names its direction count
